answer: Each identity runs a public time server whose kernel timestamps replies to random verifier polls. Its GPS-disciplined oscillator leaves a unique drift curve — offset, jitter and holdover in outages — hashed weekly against the registry; cloned hosts share one curve and merge into one slot. A terrace gateway uses it to sync tide tables; two missed polls or a duplicated curve revokes entry. 1,000 Sybils need 1,000 oscillators at $180 each plus $28 monthly hosting each ($28,000 a month). Trade-off: network partitions mimic drift, so honest hosts need an appeal window.
